issues.sym: A thump or metallic clunk when the automatic changes gear, rough downshifts, and now and then a delay before it engages, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Shift control on these automatics can produce firm, poorly timed shifts. Dodge released updated transmission control software for the complaint.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for stored codes and transmission software updates, and have the fluid level checked.

issues.t: Front wheel spindle nut may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or looseness from a front wheel, a wobble, or in the worst case the wheel coming away from the car.
issues.why: The nut holding the front wheel hub to the spindle may not have been tightened correctly, so the wheel and tire could separate while driving.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If a front wheel clunks or feels loose, stop driving and have it towed in.

issues.t: Key can come out before the car is in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key fob can be pulled from the ignition while the shifter is not in Park.
issues.why: A fault in the wireless ignition node module let the key be removed out of Park, so the car could roll away after the driver leaves.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. Until it is fixed, always confirm the car is in Park and set the parking brake before getting out.

issues.t: Power steering hose can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking in the engine bay, a burning smell, smoke from under the hood, or a whining pump from low fluid.
issues.why: The crimped end of the power steering pressure hose can separate. Fluid that sprays onto hot engine parts could catch fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for this recall. If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, pull over, shut the engine off and do not drive until it is repaired.

issues.sym: Battery light or several warning lights at once, dimming electrics, a burning smell, then stalling or a no-start. Some owners reported smoke.
issues.why: The 160-amp alternator on the V6 could fail internally without warning, cutting power and stalling the engine. Chrysler recalled it and later expanded the campaign.
issues.next: Check the VIN for both recalls. If the battery light comes on, get off the road safely; the car may stall soon.

issues.sym: Ticking from the driver's side of the engine, misfire, rough running, a flashing or steady check engine light, and sometimes stalling.
issues.why: Early versions of the left cylinder head could crack. Chrysler extended the warranty on the left head and changed the design in late 2012.
issues.next: Have a misfire or new ticking checked promptly; driving with a flashing check engine light can damage the catalytic converter. Ask a dealer whether the extended head coverage still applies.

issues.sym: Engine cranks but will not start or does not crank at all, the horn or wipers act on their own, power windows stop working, or random electrical faults.
issues.why: The Totally Integrated Power Module, which routes power to many circuits, can develop internal faults.
issues.next: Have the module diagnosed before replacing other parts like the starter or fuel pump. Check for any recalls or service programs that apply.

issues.t: Cruise control may not turn off (recall)
issues.sym: Cruise control stays on when you press the brake or the cancel button, and the car may hold speed or speed up.
issues.why: A wiring short while cruise control is on could stop the system from switching off. Chrysler recalled the cars for a software update.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and avoid using cruise control until it is done. If it will not cancel, brake firmly, shift to Neutral and stop safely.
